name: Atlassian Suite
description: Manages Atlassian credentials and identity handles (email, Jira base URL, Bitbucket workspace, Bitbucket username, Jira account id, a single Jira token plus an ordered list of Bitbucket API tokens with round-robin failover, all in SecretStorage) and exposes live Jira/Bitbucket REST probes that power ticket-existence checks, open-PR lookups, and per-token validation. Answers natural language sprint and board questions by forming JQL and querying Jira read only via the Atlassian MCP, and creates Bitbucket pull requests behind a confirmation gate. Also contributes the one Jira write Ghola permits — POSTing a comment to an existing issue, off by default behind the Enable Jira Comment Write setting, and once enabled still TPM-only, never autonomous, and gated on the operator approving the exact comment text. Post only: no editing, deleting, transitioning, or issue creation.

email.label: Atlassian Email
email.description: Email address tied to your Atlassian account. Used to authenticate live Jira and Bitbucket API requests — ticket verification and PR lookups run against this identity. The API token paired with this email is stored separately in VS Code's SecretStorage and managed from this module's panel — it is not entered here.

jiraBase.label: Jira Base URL
jiraBase.description: Base URL used to form Jira ticket links: <jiraBase>/browse/<KEY>. Trailing slashes are stripped automatically. Change this if your Atlassian instance lives at a non-default domain.

bitbucketWorkspace.label: Bitbucket Workspace
bitbucketWorkspace.description: Bitbucket Cloud workspace slug (the organization slug, e.g. herzog-technologies) that scopes every branch and PR lookup. When set, this value takes priority; leave it blank to auto-detect the slug from origin's git remote URL. CRITICAL: a wrong or renamed slug makes find-pr query the wrong workspace and silently report no PR even when one exists — if PR lookups come up empty, verify this matches your actual Bitbucket workspace.

bitbucketUsername.label: Bitbucket Username
bitbucketUsername.description: The operator's Bitbucket account username/nickname (the handle, not the display name), used to detect REVIEW mode: when the open PR's author is NOT this handle, the session is reviewing someone else's work rather than authoring. Empty disables identity-based review detection (falls back to the git-author heuristic). This is a non-secret identifier, not a credential.

jiraAccountId.label: Jira Account / Username
jiraAccountId.description: The operator's Jira account identifier. Reserved for future identity-based review detection via ticket assignee/reporter; not yet wired. Optional.

boardId.label: Board Id
boardId.description: The Jira agile board whose active sprint is queried. Leave empty to query by project and openSprints without a specific board.

boardUrl.label: Board URL
boardUrl.description: Optional board URL referenced in answers so the user can open the board directly.

resultFormat.label: Result Format
resultFormat.description: How results are presented: a compact table, grouped by status or assignee, or a plain list.

includeDoneInSprintView.label: Include Done In Sprint View
includeDoneInSprintView.description: Whether a general what is in the sprint answer includes Done items or focuses on active work.

defaultTargetBranch.label: Default PR Target Branch
defaultTargetBranch.description: The branch new pull requests target when you run the create pr verb, e.g. dev. Leave empty to be asked for the target branch each time.

createAsDraft.label: Create PRs as Draft
createAsDraft.description: When on, new pull requests are created as drafts so you can mark them ready for review after prep. Turn off to create ready-for-review PRs directly.

enableJiraCommentWrite.label: Enable Jira Comment Write
enableJiraCommentWrite.description: The outer gate on this suite's one Jira write. While this is off — and off is the default — every request to post a Jira comment is refused outright, however it is phrased and whatever Require Operator Approval is set to. Turning it on grants exactly one capability: posting a new comment to an existing issue. Every other Jira mutation stays refused — creating, cloning, or transitioning an issue, assigning it, changing any field, and editing or deleting any comment including one the agent posted itself. This gate decides whether comment posting exists at all; Require Operator Approval below decides whether each individual post is previewed and confirmed first.

attributionSuffix.label: Attribution Suffix
attributionSuffix.default:
---
Posted via Ghola on behalf of the ticket owner.
attributionSuffix.description: Appended verbatim to every Jira comment this module posts, so a teammate reading the ticket can tell the comment was agent-authored rather than typed by a person. Shown to the operator as part of the approval preview, since it is part of what gets posted. Set to an empty string to disable attribution entirely — not recommended, as unattributed agent comments on a shared ticket are a transparency problem, and the operator is the one whose name is on the account.

requireOperatorApproval.label: Require Operator Approval
requireOperatorApproval.description: When on, TPM must show the operator the full, final Jira comment text and receive an explicit confirmation before posting. This is the comment-write capability's central safety gate and should be left on. It exists as a setting only so the value is visible and auditable in the panel; turning it off removes the last check between a drafted comment and a permanent, publicly-visible write on a shared ticket, and no workflow in this module is designed to run without it.

commentPolishPrompt.label: Comment Polish Prompt
commentPolishPrompt.default: Write a concise, professional Jira comment stating the update plainly. No hedging, no double-dashes, no severity ratings.
commentPolishPrompt.description: The instruction TPM applies when drafting a Jira comment body from raw session material (a SWE report, a QA verdict, a status update). Governs tone and shape only — it never changes the approval gate, and the operator always sees and approves the final text the prompt produced.
